docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Environmental safeguards must be considered for data center locations.

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Areas susceptible to flooding and floodplains must be avoided. (ENV01.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Production and storage facilities or pipelines which are at risk of explosion must be avoided. (ENV02.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Operating and storage facilities with harmful emissions or the release of pollutants must be avoided. (ENV03.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Sources of electromagnetic interference must be avoided. (ENV04.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Sources of vibration must be avoided. (ENV05.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Transport routes with an increased volume of hazardous materials must be avoided. (ENV06.01, ENV06.01I)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Properties in the neighborhood which are at risk of being attacked must be avoided. (ENV07.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Locations in the vicinity of major events and access routes leading to them must be avoided. (ENV08.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Locations must be protected against impairment by structures at risk of collapse. (ENV09.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Locations must be outside avalanche areas. (ENV10.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Wildfire hazards must be avoided (ENV11.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Data center locations must meet the following constructional criteria:

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Security areas must be in inconspicuous, unexposed position. (CON01.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Building areas with potential hazards must be avoided. (CON01.02)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Contiguous security areas must exist. (CON01.03)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: There must be a functional room layout with fire separation. (CON01.04)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Area, height, structural properties, and transportation routes must be sufficiently dimensioned. (CON01.05)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Areas of responsibility for the technical and IT personnel must be physically separated. (CON01.06)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Perimeter and front area must be secured. (CON01.08)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Parking opportunities must not exist along the external walls of IT rooms. (CON01.09)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Alternative access routes must be available. (CON01.10A)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Reserved areas must be provided if the concept of operation provides for the temporary use of technical installations. (CON01.11)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Renting parts of the data center to a third party must be limited. (CON02.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Data center buildings must have a lightning protection system. (CON03.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Data center buildings must have a protective type of construction. (CON04.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: IT zones must have intrusion resistant security boundaries. (CON04.02)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Technical zones must be secured in accordance with EN 1627. (CON04.03)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Windows in the security area must be avoided. (CON04.04)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: All access possibilities for individuals to IT and technical rooms must be secured. (CON04.05)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Transfer points of supply networks and outdoor installations must be protected. (CON04.06)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: A protective zone shell model must be implemented. (CON04.07A)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Outer protection zone boundaries must be implemented. (CON04.08A)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Combustible finishing materials and furnishings must be avoided. (CON05.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Doors, windows, and shutters must be secured against fire and smoke. (CON05.02)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Fire stops must be properly executed. (CON05.03)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Compliance with temperature and humidity limits must be ensured in the case of ambient fires. (CON05.04)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Lithium-Ion batteries must be protected from fire. (CON05.05)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Photovoltaic systems must have additional protection. (CON05.06)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Critical rooms must have structural water protection. (CON06.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Liquid-carrying pipes must be protected against leaking water. (CON06.02)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Escape routes must be marked and include emergency lighting. (CON08.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Fire protection and extinguishing system requirements
control_requirement: The following criteria apply to fire protection and extinguishing system:

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Fire protection and extinguishing system requirements
control_requirement: Advanced and appropriate fire alarm systems must be used. (FIR01.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Fire protection and extinguishing system requirements
control_requirement: IT and technical areas must be monitored for fire. (FIR01.02)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Fire protection and extinguishing system requirements
control_requirement: Adjacent rooms must be monitored for fire. (FIR01.03)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Fire protection and extinguishing system requirements
control_requirement: The security area (incl. IT rooms) must have sufficient smoke detector density. (FIR01.04)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Fire protection and extinguishing system requirements
control_requirement: Smoke detector types must be relative to the form of room use. (FIR01.05)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Fire protection and extinguishing system requirements
control_requirement: Very early fire detection systems must be used. (FIR01.06)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Fire protection and extinguishing system requirements
control_requirement: CO2 portable fire extinguisher must be installed. (FIR01.07)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Fire protection and extinguishing system requirements
control_requirement: Technical rooms must be protected from fire. (FIR01.08)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Fire protection and extinguishing system requirements
control_requirement: IT rooms must have firefighting solutions in place. (FIR02.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Fire protection and extinguishing system requirements
control_requirement: Extinguishing batteries and oxygen reduction system must be monitored. (FIR02.02)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Fire protection and extinguishing system requirements
control_requirement: Extinguishing batteries and oxygen reduction system must be positioned away from hazards. (FIR02.03)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Fire protection and extinguishing system requirements
control_requirement: Fire protection dampers must be controlled via a fire alarm system signal. (FIR02.04)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Fire protection and extinguishing system requirements
control_requirement: Smoke and gas extraction systems must be controlled. (FIR02.05A)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Fire protection and extinguishing system requirements
control_requirement: Fire alarm systems, fire extinguishing systems and fire protection shutters must be maintained at least on an annual basis. (FIR03.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Security systems and organizational requirements
control_requirement: Security systems and organizational measures must meet the following criteria:

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Security systems and organizational requirements
control_requirement: An appropriate access control system using state-of-the-art technology must be used. (SEC01.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Security systems and organizational requirements
control_requirement: Central data base of the access control system must be protected. (SEC01.02)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Security systems and organizational requirements
control_requirement: Cables must be laid sabotage-protected and must be monitored. (SEC01.03)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Security systems and organizational requirements
control_requirement: Technical components of the access security system must be provided with a back-up power supply. (SEC01.04)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Security systems and organizational requirements
control_requirement: Suitable readers must be used for the access control system. (SEC01.05)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Security systems and organizational requirements
control_requirement: Identification devices (IDD) of the access control system must be issued and used in a secure way. (SEC01.06)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Security systems and organizational requirements
control_requirement: Access attempts through doors secured with the access control system must be logged and data must be stored for at least 30 days. (SEC01.07)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Security systems and organizational requirements
control_requirement: Besides the IDD, a second factor (knowledge or biometrics) must be used for access to IT rooms or the entire security area. (SEC01.08)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Security systems and organizational requirements
control_requirement: A security zone concept must exist. (SEC01.09)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Security systems and organizational requirements
control_requirement: Doors to rooms which are important for IT or strategically important (e.g. technical security center) must have door open time monitoring including alarm forwarding to a permanently manned office after 2 minutes. (SEC01.10)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Security systems and organizational requirements
control_requirement: An appropriate state-of-the-art intrusion detection system must be used. (SEC02.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Security systems and organizational requirements
control_requirement: Intrusion detection system in the IT areas must be equipped with motion detectors. (SEC02.03)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Security systems and organizational requirements
control_requirement: All plant rooms or the entire technical area must be monitored. (SEC02.04)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Security systems and organizational requirements
control_requirement: Access to all IT and telecommunication rooms must be incorporated into the intrusion detection system monitoring. (SEC02.05)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Security systems and organizational requirements
control_requirement: Reliable remote data transmission of the intrusion detection system must be ensured. (SEC02.06A)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Security systems and organizational requirements
control_requirement: Corridors and accesses to the IT rooms, as well as readily accessible external areas and external boundaries of the security area, must be monitored with video cameras. (SEC03.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Security systems and organizational requirements
control_requirement: Security zone borders must be monitored. (SEC04.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Security systems and organizational requirements
control_requirement: An effectively implemented single person separation system must be used to provide access to the IT area or to the entire secure area. (SEC05.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Security systems and organizational requirements
control_requirement: Components of the electronic security systems must be maintained at least annually. Components of the access control system must be inspected at least annually. (SEC06.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Security systems and organizational requirements
control_requirement: The issuance of IDD must be carried out in a formalized and transparent manner and unused access cards must be stored in a secure place. (SEC06.02)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Security systems and organizational requirements
control_requirement: Monitoring of alarms must be regulated and carried out 24/365 a year by a security service provider with a permanently manned control center. (SEC06.03)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Security systems and organizational requirements
control_requirement: Trained security personnel must be available in close proximity to the data center. (SEC06.04)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Security systems and organizational requirements
control_requirement: Optical monitoring or locking systems on the server racks that protect against unauthorized access must be installed.

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Data center cabling must meet the following criteria:

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: WAN routes as far as to the facility transfer point (external network interface) must run on separate paths without any particular hazards due to fire and mechanical influences and external network interface must be redundant. (CAB01.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: The communication cabling must run in an adequate manner. (CAB01.02E)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Telecommunication cable routing must be separated and redundant. (CAB01.03E)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Cables must be laid in an organized manner. (CAB01.04)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Rack infeed connection must be secured against accidental loosening. (CAB01.05)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Crossing points must be adequately separated. (CAB01.06E)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Data cables must be protected against sources of interference. (CAB01.07E)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Cabinets and racks must offer appropriate cable routing. (CAB02.01E)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: WAN must be supplied by at least two different providers. (CAB03.01E)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: The WAN connection must be redundant. (CAB03.02)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: The power supply in the data centers must meet the following criteria:

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: The energy supply in the building must be based on a 5-wire network and at least the IT area must be included in the TN-S structure. (POW01.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: A secondary or an additional power supply must be available in addition to the primary power supply. (POW01.02)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: The redundant connection to the mains must be either two supplies from separate and independent primary and secondary sources or two supplies from one primary source. (POW01.02A)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Primary and secondary supply lines must be routed on separate paths. (POW01.03)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Secondary of additional supply must automatically take over all critical load if the primary supply fails (and vice versa). (POW01.04)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Additional supply must be available for all supply paths. (POW01.05)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Power supply for the IT devices must be redundant. (POW01.06)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Couplings between redundant low-voltage distributions must be protected against erroneous switching operations. (POW01.07A)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Transformers must have sufficient power reserves. (POW01.08A)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Supply lines must be protected against external influences. (POW02.02)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: IT power distribution units must have their own supply line without branches. (POW02.03)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: UPS distribution boards must be without external consumers. (POW02.04)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Energy supply must have staggered overvoltage protection. (POW05.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: All electricity lines must be equipped with appropriate staggered overvoltage protection. (POW05.02)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: All metallic objects must be grounded, and floor coverings reduce the risk of electrostatic charges. (POW07.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Leakage currents must be monitored. (POW08.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Central fault current protection devices and emergency power off switches must be avoided. (POW08.02)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Important measured values of the IT supply network (e.g. voltages, currents, apparent and effective power) must be recorded and monitored. (POW08.03)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Voltage quality and design of measuring devices must be recorded and monitored. (POW08.04A)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Energy supply to the IT consumers must be secured by a central UPS. (POW09.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: UPS systems must be able to be decoupled via a manual maintenance bypass. (POW09.02)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: UPS system must have a component redundancy of n+1 or a second active supply system available. (POW09.03)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Batteries must ensure that risk of individual block failures is minimized. (POW09.07)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Additional supplies must have sufficient power reserves. (POW10.04)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Sufficient fuel reserve for additional supply must be maintained. (POW10.05)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Tank system and fuel pipes to the additional supply must be protected, controlled, and monitored. (POW10.06)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Operational readiness of the additional supply must be regularly tested by load test runs. (POW10.07)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: When the data center load is insufficient and it is therefore not possible to run the system in parallel with the mains for a function check, a load bank must be available. (POW10.07A)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Mains switching control of the additional supply must be securely installed. (POW10.08)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: A complete calculation of the load flow and short circuit currents must be carried out. (POW11.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Operating states of the electric power supply and the availability of the supply voltage must be monitored. (POW11.02)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Technical fault messages must be reliably transmitted to a permanently manned location. (POW11.03)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Electrical systems must be maintained at least once a year on the basis of a maintenance agreement and the performance must be logged. (POW11.04)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_requirement: Upon initial commissioning, function and integration tests under full and partial load must be carried out. Upon the exchange of systems, at least limited function and integration tests must be carried out. (POW11.05)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Air conditioning and ventilation
control_requirement: Data centers must meet the following air conditioning and ventilation criteria:

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Air conditioning and ventilation
control_requirement: Data Center areas must comply with secure operational conditions. (ACV01.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Air conditioning and ventilation
control_requirement: Data Center areas and technical components must have sufficient ventilation. (ACV01.02)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Air conditioning and ventilation
control_requirement: Devices must be installed in an airflow-optimized and hazard-free way. (ACV02.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Air conditioning and ventilation
control_requirement: Leakages must be reliably detected. (ACV03.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Air conditioning and ventilation
control_requirement: Active mechanical components (on the producer, distributor side) must be designed redundantly. (ACV04.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Air conditioning and ventilation
control_requirement: Singular cooling distribution systems or sections must be implemented in high quality and checked by extensive quality assurance measures. (ACV04.02)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Air conditioning and ventilation
control_requirement: Cooling distribution must be designed in a way that a failure of passive components does not result in a failure of the IT. (ACV04.02E, ACV04.02I)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Air conditioning and ventilation
control_requirement: The plant must be designed in a way that maintenance can be carried out to active components at any time without interruptions to operations. (ACV04.03)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Air conditioning and ventilation
control_requirement: The routes must be protected against third-party influence and fire. (ACV04.04)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Air conditioning and ventilation
control_requirement: Circulating air cooling units or comparable technology must be redundant (n+1) for IT and telecommunication rooms as well as singular UPS rooms. (ACV04.05, ACV04.05E, ACV04.05I)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Air conditioning and ventilation
control_requirement: Filtering of the room air must be sufficiently dimensioned for the IT rooms. (ACV05.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Air conditioning and ventilation
control_requirement: External air supply must be protected. (ACV05.03)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Air conditioning and ventilation
control_requirement: Components in the central mechanical room must be separated. (ACV06.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Air conditioning and ventilation
control_requirement: Cooling towers must be protected against tampering. (ACV07.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Air conditioning and ventilation
control_requirement: Cooling towers must be sufficiently dimensioned and installed in an operationally reliable way. (ACV07.02)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Air conditioning and ventilation
control_requirement: Cooling systems must be in a plan-compliant design and maintenance-friendly. (ACV08.01)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Air conditioning and ventilation
control_requirement: Components of the air-conditioning system must have secure electrical supply. (ACV09.01, ACV09.01I)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Air conditioning and ventilation
control_requirement: The water supply must be ensured at all times by a redundant connection or storage. (ACV09.02)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Air conditioning and ventilation
control_requirement: Water supply systems must be implemented in the same availability as the air conditioning systems whose supply they must ensure. (ACV09.02A)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Air conditioning and ventilation
control_requirement: After power failures, critical controls must restart automatically after power recovery. (ACV09.03)

docx_name: Data Center and Physical Protection Guideline_v.2.0
control_description: Data center security - Air conditioning and ventilation
control_requirement: When high-level controls are used, the critical subordinate units must be equipped with autonomous controls or redundant systems must operate with their own high-level controls. (ACV09.03A)

Information must be labelled considering its confidentiality and business impact.

Information must be labelled, considering its confidentiality, business impact and in accordance with the below listed labels: “Strictly Confidential” - information with a business impact classified as “Critical” and limited for the use within a very limited group of people, typically protected by regulation or law. “Confidential” - information with a business impact classified as “Major” and limited for use only by a restricted group of people. “Internal” - information with a business impact classified as “Minor” and limited for use only within the legal entities.

Information classified as “Public” (information with a business impact9 classified as “Negligible” and limited to and authorized for general use inside and outside the legal entity) and “External” (Information with a business impact9 classified as “Minor” and authorized for the use inside and outside of DBG) should be labelled.

All physical and printable electronic documents classified as “Internal” "Confidential", "Strictly Confidential" should be labelled based on the confidentiality of included information at the time when they are created and before printing.

Process(es), control(s) should be established to monitor, track and enforce applicable controls over the declassification of emails, documents ensuring proper labelling and protection. Measures must be implemented to prevent label circumvention when file formats are changed ●.

control_description: Data Crown Jewel Inventory & Data Flow Management

control_description: Data Crown Jewel Inventory & Data Flow Management
control_requirement: Data flows for each Data Crown Jewel must be documented, maintained in centralized Data Flow Registry●. Data Crown Jewels are mission-critical data whose unauthorized disclosure would cause intolerable and existential business impact. This includes but is not limited to: Regulatory Impact: Severe regulatory consequences such as the revocation of essential licenses or authorizations, making continued business operations impossible. Financial Impact: Severe financial losses that threaten the organization’s solvency or ability to continue operations. Customer and Market Trust Impact: Severe and sustained harmful customer or market reaction, e.g. significant market movements that threaten business viability. Operational Impact: Permanent or sustained disruption of critical core services and operations that prevents the organization from functioning

control_description: Data Crown Jewel Inventory & Data Flow Management
control_requirement: The inventory of Data Crown Jewels and associated Data Flow Registry must be reviewed at least annually to ensure completeness and ongoing relevance●.
It must be ensured that unauthorized data disclosure is mitigated and transferred data is protected.

Data Leakage Prevention tool and measures must be implemented to identify, monitor, and detect data leakage and protect data in transit. This must protect data against unauthorized disclosure, copying, or transmission, through risk-based approach.
Data Leakage Prevention measures for communications over email must be implemented.
Monitoring of emails must be enabled, at least based on the classification labels. Emails – especially non-labelled outbound ones – and attachments must be subject to appropriate technical controls.
DBAG and/or adopting legal entity email addresses created for externals sending strictly confidential messages must be secured by specific DLP measures mentioned above.
The maximum principle must be applied, ensuring that the overall classification for email reflects the highest sensitivity of any contained component wherever possible●.

DLP Endpoint protection must be implemented to protect workstation devices and user equipment from data leakage, restricting the use of removable storage media by default, subject only to temporary, monitored exceptions based on legitimate need.

All hardware and activation of ports that can be used for connection of storage media must be blocked. The necessary ports to use storage media must be enabled temporarily only if there is a business, technical or operational need, unless there is no other data access solution and exception process must be established, implemented●.

Standard software images must be designed and implemented for all workstation devices of legal entities, ensuring that ports for storage media connections are deactivated, anti-malware protection is in place, and administrator rights for users are disabled.
If there is a need to use removable storage media, transfer of information to such storage media must be monitored.

control_description: Data Leakage Prevention for online and instant messaging services

control_description: Data Leakage Prevention for online and instant messaging services

control_description: Data Leakage Prevention for online and instant messaging services
