control_requirement: It must be ensured that the legal entity is always kept up to date with regard to vulnerabilities and emerging threats.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: To raise and maintain awareness of vulnerabilities and existing or emerging threats, relevant and trusted sources of information must be regularly identified, collected, analyzed and kept up to date.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Threat intelligence should include up-to-date information about threats and attacks on strategic, tactical, and operational levels: Exchange of high-level information about the changing threat landscape (strategic level) Information about attacker methodologies, tools and technologies involved (tactical level) Details about specific attacks, including technical indicators (operational level)

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Internal and external potential threats must be collected, monitored and analyzed, taking into account attack scenarios commonly used by threat actors and scenarios based on threat intelligence.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Capabilities and staff must be in place to perform threat intelligence and analyze the impact of vulnerabilities, cyber threats and attacks on the digital operational resilience (DOR).

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Identification of vulnerabilities through fundamental and advanced tests
control_requirement: It must be ensured that both fundamental and advanced tests are properly performed to identify and evaluate vulnerabilities.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Identification of vulnerabilities through fundamental and advanced tests
control_requirement: Vulnerability identification measures must be defined and implemented for IT Assets of the legal entity in a risk-based approach that utilizes adequate assessment and test frequencies and an adequate depth and completeness of assessment and test results per Segregation Area, system criticality with regard to any of the protection goals or system purpose.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Identification of vulnerabilities through fundamental and advanced tests
control_requirement: To identify and evaluate vulnerabilities, security assessments and tests must be conducted regularly as part of the fundamental tests and, if necessary, additionally on an ad-hoc basis. The security assessment and test type (vulnerability assessments and scans, external attack surface scans, source code review and open-source analysis, network security assessments, gap analyses, physical security reviews, questionnaires and scanning software solutions, scenario-based tests, compatibility testing, performance testing, end-to-end testing and penetration testing) must be chosen based on the information asset classification with regard to any of the protection goals, asset type, exposure and the Segregation Area. For internet exposed assets, external attack surface scans should be considered.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Identification of vulnerabilities through fundamental and advanced tests
control_requirement: The vulnerability categories and assessment method as well as scope must be defined for all fundamental tests that are defined in this Guideline.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Identification of vulnerabilities through fundamental and advanced tests
control_requirement: If adverse effects are envisioned in the Red Segregation Area, fundamental tests must generally be conducted in the Yellow Segregation Area and only be conducted in other Segregation Areas if it is not possible in the Yellow Segregation Area.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Identification of vulnerabilities through fundamental and advanced tests
control_requirement: A security assessment plan must be defined to ensure that the fundamental tests of all IT Assets of the legal entity are scheduled and performed as required.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Identification of vulnerabilities through fundamental and advanced tests
control_requirement: Fundamental tests must be conducted by qualified testers that are independent from the security control implementation.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Identification of vulnerabilities through fundamental and advanced tests
control_requirement: Appropriate guiding procedures for all fundamental and advanced tests must be defined and documented.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Identification of vulnerabilities through fundamental and advanced tests
control_requirement: Processes for all fundamental and advanced tests must be defined, regularly monitored, and evaluated, for planning and conducting the fundamental and advanced tests to ensure asset coverage, appropriate scoping, timely completion, and reporting.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Identification of vulnerabilities through fundamental and advanced tests
control_requirement: Network security assessments must be conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of network security controls, identify misconfigurations, and detect potential vulnerabilities in the network architecture, including network segmentation, firewall rules, access controls, and network service configurations.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Identification of vulnerabilities through fundamental and advanced tests
control_requirement: Gap analyses must be conducted to systematically identify and document deviations between the current implementation of ICT security controls and the requirements defined in the ICT Risk Management Framework, applicable regulatory requirements, and the digital operational resilience strategy.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Identification of vulnerabilities through fundamental and advanced tests
control_requirement: Questionnaires must be used as a structured assessment method to evaluate the ICT security posture of the legal entity and of ICT third-party service providers where direct technical testing is not feasible, in accordance with ID 2 (Vulnerability management of ICT third-party service providers).

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: It must be ensured that as part of the security assessments and tests, penetration tests are performed.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Penetration tests must be performed regularly at the defined intervals:

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Penetration tests of all IT applications and their underlying infrastructure assets supporting critical (regarding confidentiality, integrity, availability, or authenticity) or important functions (CIF) and of all KRITIS-relevant assets must be conducted at least every 12 months.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Penetration tests of all internet-facing IT applications and their underlying infrastructure assets must be conducted at least every 12 months.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Penetration tests of all IT Applications and their underlying infrastructure assets that are critical regarding confidentiality, integrity, availability, or authenticity must be conducted at least every 12 months.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Penetration tests of all other IT Applications and their underlying infrastructure assets infrastructure (that are not covered by 5.1.1.-5.1.3) must be conducted at least every 36 months.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Penetration tests of all IT applications and their underlying infrastructure assets must be conducted upfront before initial deployment into the Red Segregation Area, and whenever security relevant changes are released into the Red Segregation Area.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: If network segments (within a network security zone) are segregated, the frequency of penetration tests must be based on the maximum criticality value (regarding confidentiality, integrity, availability, or authenticity) of the assets in the respective segregated network segment within that network security zone.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: If network segments (within a network security zone) are not segregated, the frequency of penetration tests for all applications within these unsegregated network segments must be determined based on the maximum criticality value (regarding confidentiality, integrity, availability, or authenticity) of the assets in the respective network segments within that network security zone.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Penetration tests must be carried out by independent testers with sufficient knowledge, skills, and expertise in testing information security measures and who are not involved in the development of the information security measures.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Vendor rotation must be applied at least every 24 months.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Penetration tests for software as a service (SaaS) provided by third parties must be conducted by the vendor according to contractual agreements based on the requirements for internet-facing IT applications (see above).

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Type, scope, period, and results of a penetration test must be documented in a traceable manner which is comprehensible for a competent third party.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: All detected vulnerabilities must be transferred and addressed to a predefined structured remediation process.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: A combination of blackbox and greybox testing should be conducted.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: It must be ensured that as part of the security assessments and tests, vulnerability assessments and scans are performed.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Prior to their deployment, all IT Assets with the exception of Mobile Devices must be onboarded to the vulnerability scanning tool(s).

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Prior to their deployment or redeployment in the Red Segregation Area, vulnerability assessments must be performed on all IT Assets and ICT services that support critical or important functions.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Regular automated vulnerability scans and assessments on all relevant IT Assets must be performed, with the frequency and scope corresponding to their information classification with regards to any of the protection goals and overall risk profile of the IT Asset, however at least weekly.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Source code review and open-source analysis
control_requirement: It must be ensured that as part of the security assessments and tests, source code reviews and open-source analysis are performed.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Source code review and open-source analysis
control_requirement: Source code review must be conducted for all source codes of IT applications before deployment in the Red Segregation Area.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Source code review and open-source analysis
control_requirement: Source code reviews must be conducted for all owned source codes of IT applications at least every 12 months.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Source code review and open-source analysis
control_requirement: Source code reviews for not owned source code of IT applications must be performed by the external vendor. Reports or confirmations must be conducted.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Source code review and open-source analysis
control_requirement: The use of third-party libraries, including open-source libraries used by ICT services supporting critical or important functions, as well as ICT services developed by the legal entity or customized or specifically developed for the legal entity by ICT third-party service providers, must be monitored, also with respect to new updates, tracked and controlled.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Source code review and open-source analysis
control_requirement: For IT Assets used in the operation of ICT services that do not support critical or important functions, the use of third-party libraries, including open-source libraries, must be tracked to the extent possible.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: As part of the security assessments and tests, compliance scans must be conducted for IT Asset at least weekly and should be conducted on an on-going basis for End User Devices.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The legal entity should consider bug bounty programs with clearly defined rules and scope, where rewards are offered as an incentive to assist legal entities in identifying vulnerabilities in order to appropriately remediate them.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: General requirements for advanced testing based on TLPT
control_requirement: It must be ensured that advanced tests, which mimic the tactics, techniques and procedures of real-life threat actors are carried out.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: General requirements for advanced testing based on TLPT
control_requirement: TLPTs must be carried out at least every three years, with the interval adjusted as requested by the competent authority.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: General requirements for advanced testing based on TLPT
control_requirement: Each TLPT must cover several critical or important functions of the legal entity and must be performed in the Red Segregation Area.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: General requirements for advanced testing based on TLPT
control_requirement: For this purpose, all relevant underlying ICT Systems, processes, and technologies that support these critical or important functions and ICT services, including those outsourced to third-party providers, must be identified.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: General requirements for advanced testing based on TLPT
control_requirement: The legal entity must assess which critical or important functions need to be covered by the TLPT, thereby determining the precise scope of the TLPT, which must then be validated by the competent authority.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: It must be ensured that organizational and procedural measures are taken, and a control team lead is assigned to safeguard the proper execution of TLPTs.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The legal entity must appoint a control team lead responsible for the day-to-day management of the TLPT, as well as the decisions and actions of the control team.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The legal entity must establish both organizational and procedural measures to ensure the following:

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Access to information regarding a planned or ongoing TLPT is limited based on the need-to-know principle to the control team, management body, testers, threat intelligence provider, and the TLPT authority.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The control team must consult the test managers before involving a member of the blue team in a TLPT.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The control team must be informed of any relevant detection of the TLPT by staff members of the legal entity or third-party service providers, with the control team being responsible for the escalation of the resulting incident response, where required.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Confidentiality agreements must be in place for the legal entity's staff involved in the TLPTs and the relevant third-party ICT service providers, testers, and threat intelligence providers.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The control team must provide any information relating to the TLPT to the test managers on request.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Wherever possible, parties involved in the TLPT must refer to it only by its code name.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: It must be ensured that in the case of pooled and joint TLPTs, each legal or financial entity is itself responsible for risk management in relation to TLPTs.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: When performing a joint or pooled TLPT, the control team of each legal or financial entity must:

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Conduct its own risk assessment and establish its own risk management measures.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Consider aspects related to the involvement of multiple financial entities in the TLPT for the risk assessment.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Follow each of the requirements related to TLPT, including providing the remediation plan to the TLPT authority, as referred to in the control requirement for Remediation of Vulnerabilities.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: If multiple TLPT authorities are involved in a joint or pooled TLPT, the term "TLPT authority" must be understood as referring to the leading TLPT authority.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: If the participation of an ICT third-party service provider in the TLPT is expected to negatively impact the quality, security, or confidentiality of services provided to other customers, the legal entity and the provider must agree in writing for the provider to contract directly with an external tester allowing pooled testing. The pooled TLPT must cover the relevant ICT services supporting critical or important functions provided by the ICT third-party service provider to those financial entities. The number of financial entities participating in pooled TLPT shall be calibrated based on the complexity and type of ICT services involved.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: During the preparation phase, it must be ensured that timelines are adhered to, specific documentation is created and made available to relevant stakeholders, and that stakeholders are involved accordingly.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Within three months of receiving notification from the TLPT authority that a TLPT is to be conducted, the legal entity must submit the following TLPT initiation documents to the test managers: A project charter, including a high-level project plan, containing the information set out in Annex I of the DORA RTS on TLPT The contact details of the control team lead Information on the intended use of internal or external testers, or both Information on the communication channels to be used during the TLPT The code name for the TLPT

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: After the validation of the TLPT initiation documents by the TLPT authority, a control team must be established to support the control team lead in the following tasks: Defining communication channels and processes within the control team, as well as with the testers and threat intelligence providers, on all matters related to the TLPT Informing the management body of the legal entity about the progress of the TLPT and the associated risks Making decisions based on subject matter expertise throughout the TLPT Selecting the threat intelligence provider and the external testers, internal testers, or both for the TLPT Preparing the scope specification document

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The legal entity must submit a scope specification document containing all the information set out in Annex II of the RTS on TLPT to the test managers within six months of receiving notification from the TLPT authority requesting that a TLPT be carried out. The management body of the financial entity shall approve the scope specification document.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Once contracted, the control team must share the initiation documents and scope specification document with the testers and threat intelligence providers and inform them about the testing process to be followed.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The procurement or assignment of testers and threat intelligence providers must be finalized before the testing phase begins.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Risk assessment and management associated with TLPTs
control_requirement: It must be ensured that during the preparation phase the control team adequately assesses risks associated with TLPTs.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Risk assessment and management associated with TLPTs
control_requirement: All of the following must be considered for the inclusion of critical or important functions in the scope of the TLPT: Criticality or importance of the function and its possible impact to the financial sector and on financial stability at national and Union level Importance of the function for the day-to-day business operations of the legal entity Exchangeability of the function Interdependence with other functions Geographical location of the function Sectoral dependence of other entities on the function Threat intelligence concerning the function, where available

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Risk assessment and management associated with TLPTs
control_requirement: The control team must consult the test managers on the TLPT risk assessment and risk management measures prior to initiating the testing phase. Additionally, they must review the risk assessment and risk management measures if the TLPT authority determines that they do not adequately address the risks of the TLPT.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Risk assessment and management associated with TLPTs
control_requirement: The control team must at least consider the following types of risks in their risk assessment and management: Granting the threat intelligence provider and external testers access to sensitive and confidential information Non-compliance of the TLPT with the requirements laid out in this Guideline, including breaches of confidentiality or lack of ethical conduct Crisis and incident escalation Activities of the red or blue team, including risks associated with the disruption of critical activities and corruption of data due to the activities of the testers or the blue team and potential impacts on third parties Incomplete restoration of systems affected by the TLPT

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Risk assessment and management associated with TLPTs
control_requirement: Effective risk management controls must be applied, with the cooperation of ICT third-party service providers and involved parties (excluding competent authorities), to mitigate the risks of potential impact on data, damage to assets, and disruption of critical or important functions, services, or operations within the legal entity, its counterparts, or the financial sector.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Requirements for TLPT testers and threat intelligence providers
control_requirement: During the preparation phase, the control team must ensure that the testers contracted and involved in the TLPTs, including internal testers and threat intelligence providers, are suitably qualified.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Requirements for TLPT testers and threat intelligence providers
control_requirement: Only testers, whether internal or external, that meet all the following must be used to perform the TLPTs: Demonstration of highest suitability and reputability Possess technical and organizational capabilities and show specific expertise in threat intelligence, penetration testing, and red team testing Be certified by an accreditation body in a Member State or adhere to formal codes of conduct or ethical frameworks Provide independent assurance or an audit report regarding the sound management of risks associated with conducting the TLPT, including appropriate protection of the legal entity's confidential information and redress for business risks Be fully and duly covered by relevant professional indemnity insurances that cover risks of misconduct and negligence. Threat intelligence providers must also have such insurance

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Requirements for TLPT testers and threat intelligence providers
control_requirement: If internal testers are used, all the following must additionally be fulfilled: Internal testers must be approved by the relevant competent authority or the single public authority The legal entity must have sufficient dedicated resources and capabilities when using internal testers, as verified by the competent TLPT authority, and must ensure that conflicts of interest are avoided throughout all phases of the TLPT, especially during the design and execution phases Measures must be taken to ensure that using internal testers does not adversely affect the legal entity's overall defensive or resilience capabilities with respect to ICT-related incidents, or significantly impact the availability of resources devoted to ICT-related tasks during a TLPT The threat intelligence provider must always be external The internal testing team includes a test lead, and at least two additional members All members of the test team have been employed by the financial entity or by an ICT intra-group service provider for the preceding 12 months;

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Requirements for TLPT testers and threat intelligence providers
control_requirement: The use of internal testers must be mentioned in all the following documents: The test initiation documents The red team test report The report summarizing the relevant findings of the TLPT

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Requirements for TLPT testers and threat intelligence providers
control_requirement: Testers employed by an ICT intra-group service provider must be regarded as internal testers of the legal entity.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Requirements for TLPT testers and threat intelligence providers
control_requirement: When using internal testers for TLPT, external testers must be contracted every three tests.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Requirements for TLPT testers and threat intelligence providers
control_requirement: Contracts with external testers must ensure that the TLPT results are properly managed and that any data processing, including generation, storage, aggregation, drafting, reporting, communication, or destruction, does not introduce risks to the legal entity.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Requirements for TLPT testers and threat intelligence providers
control_requirement: For external testers, the staff of the red team assigned to the TLPT must: Consist of at least one manager with at least five years' experience and at least two additional testers with at least two years' experience of penetration and red team testing each Possess a broad and suitable level of professional knowledge and skills, including understanding the legal entity's business, reconnaissance, risk management, exploit development, physical penetration, social engineering, vulnerability analysis, and adequate communication skills to clearly present the results Have participated in a minimum of five previous penetration and red team testing engagements Not be employed by, or provide services to, a provider that simultaneously performs blue team functions for any financial institution, ICT third-party service provider, or intragroup ICT service provider participating in the TLPT Be separated from any employee of the same vendor who is also providing threat intelligence services to the same TLPT

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Requirements for TLPT testers and threat intelligence providers
control_requirement: The staff of the threat intelligence provider assigned to the TLPT must: Consist of at least one manager with a minimum of five years' experience and at least one other member with at least two years' experience in threat intelligence Possess a broad and suitable level of professional knowledge and skills, including intelligence gathering tactics, techniques and procedures, geopolitical, technical, and sectoral knowledge, and adequate communication skills to clearly present and report on the outcome of the assignment Have participated in a minimum of three previous threat intelligence engagements involving penetration and red team testing Not simultaneously perform blue team duties or other services that may present a conflict of interest with the legal entity, ICT third-party service provider or intragroup ICT service provider involved in the TLPT Be separated from, and not report to, personnel from the same vendor providing external testers for the same TLPT

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Requirements for TLPT testers and threat intelligence providers
control_requirement: Both threat intelligence providers and external testers must supply copies of certifications that meet recognized market standards and demonstrate their suitability for performing their respective activities.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Requirements for TLPT testers and threat intelligence providers
control_requirement: External testers must provide at least five references from previous assignments related to penetration and red team testing.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Requirements for TLPT testers and threat intelligence providers
control_requirement: Threat intelligence providers must provide at least three references from previous assignments related to penetration and red team testing.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Requirements for TLPT testers and threat intelligence providers
control_requirement: Measures and safeguards must be taken to ensure the participation of ICT third-party service providers if involved in the TLPT. The legal entity remains fully responsible for compliance with this Guideline.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Requirements for TLPT testers and threat intelligence providers
control_requirement: The control team must keep records of the documentation provided by the testers and threat intelligence providers, including their curriculum vitae, as evidence of compliance with the requirements set out in this Guideline.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Requirements for TLPT testers and threat intelligence providers
control_requirement: External testers and threat intelligence providers that do not fulfil one or more of the relevant requirements specified in this Guideline must only be contracted in exceptional cases. In such instances, the legal entity must take and document appropriate measures to mitigate the risks associated with non-compliance with those requirements.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Requirements for TLPT testers and threat intelligence providers
control_requirement: The control team must assess whether the threat intelligence providers and testers intended for the TLPT meet the relevant requirements, document the outcome of this assessment, and select providers based on this assessment and their risk management practices.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Requirements for TLPT testers and threat intelligence providers
control_requirement: Before contracting threat intelligence providers and external testers, the control team must provide evidence of compliance with the relevant requirements specified in this Guideline to the test managers.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Requirements for TLPT testers and threat intelligence providers
control_requirement: Threat intelligence providers or external testers must not be contracted if the TLPT authority determines that they do not comply with national security legislation or lack the necessary qualifications.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Following the approval of the scope specification document by the TLPT authority, it must be ensured during the testing phase that the threat intelligence provider provides relevant information and that appropriate scenarios are selected for the TLPT.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The threat intelligence provider must analyze generic and sector-specific threat intelligence, identify cyber threats and existing or potential vulnerabilities relevant to the legal entity, and collect and analyze specific, actionable, and contextualized target and threat intelligence relating to the legal entity. This must include consultation with the control team and test managers.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The threat intelligence provider must present the relevant threats and targeted threat intelligence and propose appropriate scenarios to the control team, testers, and managers. The proposed scenarios must vary in terms of the identified threat actors and associated tactics, techniques, and procedures, and must target each of the critical or important functions within the scope of the TLPT.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The control team lead must select a minimum of three scenarios to conduct the TLPT based on the following elements: The recommendation of the threat intelligence provider and the threat-led nature of each scenario The input provided by the test managers The feasibility of the proposed scenarios, based on the expert judgement of the testers The size, complexity, and overall risk profile of the legal entity, as well as the nature, scale, and complexity of its services, activities, and operations

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The selected scenarios must fulfil all of the following:

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: At most, only one of the selected scenarios must be non-threat-led and instead be based on a forward-looking and potentially fictitious threat, considering the expected developments in the threat landscape.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: When performing a pooled TLPT, at least one scenario must cover relevant underlying ICT Systems, processes, and technologies of the ICT third-party service provider that support the critical or important functions within the scope of the TLPT. For a joint TLPT with an ICT intra-group service provider, the scenario must cover the ICT Systems, processes, and technologies of the intra-group service provider.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The threat intelligence provider must provide the control team with the targeted threat intelligence report, which includes the information outlined in Annex III of the RTS on TLPT and the selected scenarios.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The control team must submit the targeted threat intelligence report to the test manager for approval, and the control team lead shall be informed once the report is validated.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: During the testing phase, it must be ensured that a red team test plan is agreed upon and that the subsequent testing activities are conducted in accordance with this plan and other relevant requirements.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Once the TLPT authority approves the targeted threat intelligence report, the testers must prepare the red team test plan, including the information outlined in Annex IV of the RTS on TLPT. They must use the approved threat intelligence report and the scope specification document as the basis for developing the attack scenarios.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The testers must consult with the control team, threat intelligence provider, and test managers on the red team test plan. This includes communication, operational and project management arrangements, preparation and use cases for activating leg-ups, as well as reporting arrangements to the control team and test managers.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The red team test plan must be approved by the control team and the TLPT authority.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Any subsequent changes to the red team test plan, including schedule, scope, target systems, or flags, must be approved by both the control team lead and the test managers.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Once the red team test plan is approved by both the control team and the TLPT authority, the testers must carry out the TLPT during the active red team testing phase.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: While the active red team testing phase must be conducted for a minimum of 12 weeks, any additional duration must be proportionate to the scope of the TLPT and reflect the size, activity, complexity, and number of financial institutions and ICT third parties or intra-group ICT service providers involved.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The control team, threat intelligence provider, testers, and test managers must all agree on the conclusion of the active red team testing phase.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Throughout the active red team testing phase, the testers must update the control team and test managers on the status of the TLPT at least weekly.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: During the entire active red team testing phase, the threat intelligence provider must be available for consultation and to provide additional threat intelligence as requested by the control team.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The control team must provide in a timely manner leg-ups, designed based on the red team test plan, to help overcome obstacles and ensure that the exercise remains within the time constraints. These leg-ups may be added or modified with the approval of the control team and the test managers.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: If an employee of the legal entity or one of its ICT third-party service providers or intra-group ICT service providers discovers the testing activities, the control team, in coordination with the testers, must propose and submit measures to the test managers for validation. These measures must enable the continuation of the TLPT while maintaining its confidentiality.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Only in exceptional circumstances that pose a risk of harm to data, damage to assets, or disruption of critical or important functions, services, or operations - whether belonging to the legal entity, its ICT third-party service providers, its intra-group ICT service providers or impacting its counterparties or the financial sector - the control team lead must temporarily suspend the TLPT. As a final resort, if continuing the TLPT is impossible and with prior validation from the TLPT authority, the control team lead must proceed with a limited purple teaming exercise, whose duration counts towards the minimum 12-week active red team testing phase.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: It must be ensured that the parties involved in the TLPT do not carry out any prohibited activities during the testing phase.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The testers and threat intelligence providers must be prohibited from the following activities:

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Unauthorized destruction of equipment and modification of information and IT Assets of the legal entity or its ICT third-party service providers.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Intentional disruption of the continuity of critical or important functions of the legal entity.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Unauthorized inclusion of ICT Systems outside the scope of the TLPT.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Unauthorized disclosure of test results.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Once the active red team testing phase has been completed, it must be ensured that the closure phase is initiated, relevant reports are submitted and required exercises are being performed.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: At the end of the active red team testing phase, the control team lead must inform the blue team that a TLPT has taken place. The control team must then promptly provide the red team test report to the blue team and test managers.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Within four weeks of completing the active red team testing phase, the testers must provide the control team with a red team test report, as detailed in Annex V of the RTS on TLPT.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: After getting the red team test report, and within ten weeks of finishing the active red team test phase, the blue team must give the control team a blue test report with the details specified in Annex VI of the RTS on TLPT.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The control team must promptly provide the blue team's test report to the testers and test managers.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: If requested by the test managers, the red and blue team test reports must not include any sensitive information.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Within ten weeks of finishing the active red team testing phase, the blue team and testers must replay the offensive and defensive actions from the TLPT. Additionally, the control team must carry out purple teaming exercises on topics chosen by the blue team and testers, focusing on identified vulnerabilities and any issues not tested during the active red team phase.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: After completing the replay and purple teaming exercises, the control team, blue team, testers, and threat intelligence providers must give feedback to each other on the TLPT process.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: After the TLPT authority informs the control team lead that the blue and red team test reports are satisfactory, the legal entity and any external testers must submit a summary report to the TLPT authority and the competent authority, if different, within eight weeks. This report must include the TLPT findings, as stated in Annex VII of the RTS on TLPT, remediation plans, as outlined in the control requirement Remediation of vulnerabilities, and documentation showing the TLPT was conducted properly.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Once the active red team testing phase has been completed, it must be ensured that the recovery procedures are carried out.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: At the end of the testing activities, the testers and threat intelligence providers must carry out restoration procedures. These procedures must include securely deleting compromised passwords, credentials, and other secret keys, securely communicating compromised accounts to the legal entity, and securely handling the collection, storage, management, and disposal of collected data.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Additionally, testers must perform the following restoration procedures: Deactivating command and control Scope and date kill switch(es) Removing backdoors and other malware Notifying relevant parties of potential breaches Procedures for future restoration of backups that may contain malware or tools installed during the test Monitoring blue team activities and informing the control team of any detections

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: It must be ensured that identified vulnerabilities and associated risks are carefully and appropriately evaluated.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The severity and risks associated with detected vulnerabilities must be determined without undue delay after detection.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Priority of the remediation activities for each validated vulnerability must be determined by considering associated risks. To make a consistent and informed decision on priority, the vulnerability item priority must be assessed as follows:

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The output provided by scanners must be normalized and a DBG priority must be determined by additionally taking into account the exposure and criticality with regard to any of the protection goals of the asset.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The output of a quantitative scoring model must be mapped to the Vulnerability Item Priority, and the mapping must be approved by the 2nd LoD of the legal entity.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Zero-day vulnerabilities must be evaluated without undue delay, prioritized based on their exploitability, and timely treated through appropriate risk-based counter measures.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: It must be ensured that identified vulnerabilities are reported in a timely and appropriate manner to all relevant stakeholders.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Regular reporting frequency must be defined; vulnerabilities classified as “high” or above (comparable with high or above in CVSS) must immediately be reported to the respective IT Asset Owners and Information Owner.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The vulnerabilities’ risks and risk values must be included in the report.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: For an efficient reporting scheme, regular reporting and ad-hoc reporting must be in place.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Status of vulnerabilities must be regularly reported to the IT Asset Owners, at least once a month.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Total vulnerability landscape must be regularly reported to 1st LoD, DBAG CISO and LE CISOs, at least once a month.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Ad-hoc reporting must be used to inform DBAG CISO, LE CISOs of the affected LEs and IT Asset Owners about emergency and critical vulnerabilities without undue delay. Affected Information Owners and CERT (optional) must be informed about critical and emergency vulnerabilities without undue delay.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: All vulnerabilities identified in fundamental and advanced tests must be reported to the IT Asset owners, to DBAG CISO and affected LE CISOs latest two weeks after assessment completion. In case the affected IT Asset Owners cannot be identified within this timeline, the reporting timeline to these IT Asset Owners can be prolonged. In addition, affected Information Owners and CERT (optional) must be informed about critical and emergency vulnerabilities.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The red team test report must be shared with DBAG CISO and LE CISOs of the affected LEs in due course and in the event no CISO is appointed, it must be shared with the 2nd LoD.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Procedures for the responsible disclosure of vulnerabilities to clients, counterparties and to the public must be established.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: It must be ensured that identified vulnerabilities are treated in an appropriate and prioritized manner.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The vulnerabilities must be remediated according to the vulnerability item priority. The timelines for remediation (upon detection) and vulnerability item priority must be: Emergency: All critical vulnerabilities that are reported to and stated as “emergency action required” by CERT are defined as emergency vulnerabilities. Classification criteria for vulnerability item priority emergency are defined in control requirement ID 30: Without undue delay Critical: DBG score 9.0 - 10.0; max. 32 calendar days High: DBG score 7.0 - 8.9; max. 77 calendar days Medium: DBG score 4.0 - 6.9; max. 180 calendar days Low: DBG score 0.0 - 3.9; max. 360 calendar days

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: In case the remediation activities require changes on IT Assets of the legal entity, patch management as part of the change management process must be followed, irrespective whether the patch is being delivered from a vendor or development team.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: A process must be defined and documented for handling requests to extend prescribed remediation timelines.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Use cases for an exception process must be documented and defined. The Information Owners of the legal entities must approve the criteria.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Vulnerabilities that cannot be remediated must be subject to compensating controls which must follow a risk-based approach and must be documented. The residual risk must be calculated.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Remediation plans, as specified in the closure phase control requirement for TLPTs, must include all of the following for each finding identified within the TLPT: A description of the identified deficiencies A description of the proposed remediation measures, their prioritization and estimated completion, including, where appropriate, actions to improve identification, protection, detection, and response capabilities A root cause analysis The personnel or functions of the legal entity responsible for implementing the proposed remediation or improvement The risks involved in not implementing the remediation measures and, where relevant, the risks involved in implementing such measures

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The legal entity should participate in information sharing arrangements with other trustworthy financial entities.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The legal entity should share cyber threat information and intelligence, including indicators of compromise, tactics, techniques and procedures, cyber security alerts and configuration tools, with other financial entities, provided that such sharing: Enhances the digital operational resilience of the financial entities by raising awareness of cyber threats, limiting, or impeding the ability of cyber threats to propagate, and supporting defensive capabilities, threat detection techniques, mitigation strategies, or response and recovery phases Is conducted within trusted communities of financial entities Is implemented through information sharing arrangements that protect the sensitivity of the information exchanged and are governed by codes of conduct that fully respect business confidentiality and the protection of personal data

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: When participating in information sharing arrangements, the information sharing arrangements must specify conditions for participation and, where appropriate, details of the inclusion of public authorities and the capacity in which they may be involved. The arrangements must also outline the involvement of ICT third-party service providers and the operational aspects, including the use of dedicated IT platforms.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: When participating in information sharing arrangements, upon validation or cessation of membership, the legal entity must notify the competent authority.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: It must be ensured that proper patch management is in place to handle patches effectively.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Patch management procedures must be developed, documented, and implemented.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The implementation of patches must follow the formalized change process for the timely identification, prioritization, procurement, installation, and validation.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The current patch levels of all systems must be compared against patch information from the vendor to support the assessment of the current level of risk.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Any new system and third-party software must be scanned for vulnerabilities and available patches and ensure it has up-to-date patches installed before connecting to DBAGs or the legal entity's environment according to protection need. In special cases, e.g. provisioning of notebooks, patches must be applied in a timely manner after connecting to DBAG or the legal entity's network.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: It must be ensured that as part of the patch management procedures, available patches are identified in a timely manner.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Available software and hardware patches and updates, which must be installed proactively, must be identified and evaluated using automated tools wherever possible, while end-of-life and unsupported software are treated as elevated risks and reported accordingly.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Infrastructure scanners should be able to scan and identify missing patches on all network devices (wired and wireless), servers, end user devices, mobile devices.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: It must be ensured that as part of the patch management procedures, patches are deployed properly.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: To address identified vulnerabilities, within defined timelines, the deployment of patches and other mitigation measures must be prioritized following a risk-based approach based on the criticality of the vulnerability.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Prior to their deployment, patches and updates for software and hardware must be tested in accordance with the requirements laid out in the Software Development and ICT Change Management Guideline.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Adequate measures must be in place for system integrity testing after patch deployment, including rollback plans in the event that system integrity testing fails.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The Asset Owners must, if possible, use tools that support centralized patch management capabilities and automated deployment of applicable patches.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: During the patch processing within Change Management, the downloaded/delivered patch must be scanned for malware and the patch source is authenticated. The integrity of the patch must be confirmed before deployment (e.g. by verifying digital signature of the patch, hash signature comparison against the vendor publicly reported patch file hash and integrity-check).

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Exceptions for the deployment of patches
control_requirement: It must be ensured that exceptions for the deployment of patches are handled carefully, using a risk-based approach that considers the exposure and criticality of the vulnerability.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Exceptions for the deployment of patches
control_requirement: Where a patch implementation exception is required, a valid workaround to mitigate the associated vulnerabilities must be applied, if technically feasible. In cases where no such workaround or other mitigation measures can be applied, and no patch is expected to be released, a risk assessment should be conducted, and the replacement and disposal of the affected asset should be considered.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Exceptions for the deployment of patches
control_requirement: Any exception must be documented and maintained for audit purposes.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_description: Exceptions for the deployment of patches
control_requirement: Any failure to implement a patch must be formally justified and approved by the responsible Asset Owner and the applicable Risk Owner.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: It must be ensured that the remediation of identified vulnerabilities is monitored.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Every detected vulnerability affecting ICT Systems must be recorded and the remediation of vulnerabilities must be monitored and verified.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: It must be ensured that any vulnerability identified as an emergency is given special attention and that emergency procedures are in place to address it.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Vulnerabilities classified as “emergency” must follow defined vulnerability emergency management procedures, covering identified processes for the patching and updating of IT Assets.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The definition for emergency classification of vulnerabilities must at a minimum consider these criteria: Whether a vulnerability that has been classified as “emergency” in the past is found again The exploitability of the vulnerability The technical impact of the vulnerability on relevant services and IT Assets, including supporting components The exposure and criticality with regard to any of the protection goals of the affected or potentially affected IT Assets, including supporting components, and in particular affected critical or important functions (CIFs)

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: It must be ensured that escalation procedures are in place and applied when vulnerabilities are not adequately addressed.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Escalation processes must be established as part of the defined vulnerability emergency management procedures which are applied in the following cases: The vulnerability is not remediated within the given timeline, including failure to deploy patches and updates for software and hardware within the designated timeline For exceptional cases where regular remediation according to the defined requirements is considered not possible

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: Overdue vulnerabilities must be followed up on a weekly basis.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: An audit log must be kept for all steps undertaken in technical vulnerability management.

docx_name: ICT Patch and Vulnerability Management Guideline_v2.0
control_requirement: The vulnerability management process must be aligned with the incident management process to enable information and data communication for relevant vulnerabilities to the incident response function in case an incident occurs.

control_description: ICT Risk Framework and ICT Risk Management Framework
control_requirement: It must be ensured that an ICT Risk Framework is established as an integral part of the ICT Risk Management Framework.

control_description: ICT Risk Framework and ICT Risk Management Framework
control_requirement: A comprehensive ICT Risk Framework (which is part of the ICT Risk Management Framework) must be planned, established, implemented, maintained, and continually improved to align with legislative, regulatory, and contractual requirements, as well as best practices, international standards, business objectives, digital operational resilience strategy, legal entities' requirements, risk appetite, and the ICT Threat Landscape.

control_description: ICT Risk Framework and ICT Risk Management Framework
control_requirement: The ICT Risk Management Framework must include at least strategies, policies, procedures, ICT protocols and tools that are necessary to duly and adequately protect Primary and Secondary Assets from ICT risks. This also encompasses domains outside the mandate of ICT risk, such as Third-Party Risk Management or Business Continuity Management. The ICT Risk Framework specifically includes documentation of policies, guidelines and procedures (incl. supporting documents).

control_description: ICT Risk Framework and ICT Risk Management Framework
control_requirement: The stakeholders (such as DBAG Group Risk Management and legal entity risk management function) defined in the ICT Risk Management Framework (including the ICT Risk Management Policy and ICT Risk Guidelines) must be identified and adequately involved and informed about the ICT Risk Management Framework.

control_description: ICT Risk Framework and ICT Risk Management Framework
control_requirement: The ICT Risk Management Framework must be reviewed and approved at least once a year and must additionally be reviewed and approved at least after the occurrence of a major ICT-related incident and following supervisory instructions or findings resulting from relevant digital operational resilience tests or audit procedures.

control_description: ICT Risk Framework and ICT Risk Management Framework
control_requirement: The approach for monitoring, measuring, evaluating, and reporting of the ICT Risk Management Framework must be defined.

control_description: ICT Risk Framework and ICT Risk Management Framework
control_requirement: A report on the review of the ICT Risk Management Framework must follow defined minimum requirements as outlined in Dora RTS Art. 27.2 and must be submitted to the competent authority at its request in a searchable electronical format.

control_description: ICT Risk Framework and ICT Risk Management Framework
control_requirement: The ICT Risk Management Framework must be continuously improved based on the knowledge gained during implementation, monitoring, as well as from material changes, including changes to the cyber threat landscape, applicable legal obligations, ICT-related incidents and TLPTs, if relevant.

control_description: ICT Risk Framework and ICT Risk Management Framework
control_requirement: The ICT Risk Management Framework must be subjected to regular internal ICT Risk Assurance assessments.
It must be ensured that a digital operational resilience (DOR) strategy is established, monitored and maintained supporting the business strategy and objectives.

The DOR strategy must include current and target capabilities to address digital operational resilience and attain respective objectives (measured through appropriate metrics), by establishing the risk tolerance level for ICT risk, in accordance with the risk appetite of legal entities.
The DOR strategy must explain the ICT reference architecture including required changes to reach the objectives.

The DOR strategy must outline implemented mechanisms to detect ICT-related incidents (incl. major ICT-related incidents) to prevent their impact and explain, by measuring their effectiveness, how they provide appropriate protection.
The DOR strategy must explain required changes to digital operational resilience testing and how it is implemented.
The DOR strategy must outline a communication strategy in the event of ICT-related incidents which are to be disclosed.
The DOR strategy must include a procedure to monitor the execution and effectiveness of the strategy.

It must be ensured that changes to the business strategy, IT strategy and the DOR strategy are considered when developing, documenting, and implementing ICT Risk Management processes, policies, guidelines and procedures.
The DOR strategy must explain how the ICT Risk Management Framework supports the business strategy and objectives of DBAG or the respective legal entity.

The evolution of ICT risks and ICT-related incidents (incl. cyber-attacks) must be analyzed over time, considering relevant metrics (e.g. frequency, types, magnitude) or patterns to deepen the understanding of the risk exposure, especially with regards to critical or important functions, and to improve the DOR.
The current DOR situation must be evident based on the number of reported major ICT-related incidents and the effectiveness of preventive measures.
The management body must be responsible for approving the DOR strategy.
It must be ensured that control requirements in the ICT Risk Guidelines are properly defined and correspond to the protection need.

Control requirements must be formulated to reflect the asset criticality with regard to any of the protection goals, legislative statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements, as well as their role in supporting critical or important functions (CIF).
It must be ensured that information classification is performed and documented properly according to pre-defined criteria.
Information classification must reflect the highest classification value separately for each security objective of confidentiality, integrity, availability, and authenticity.

The classification process, criteria and classification results should be aligned with the business impact analysis methodology and process as well as the CIF process. It must consider the impact classification according to the table below.
Information classification must be proportionately reflected in protection level and respective control requirements must be defined for the respective Information and related Secondary Assets.
The cost of appropriately protecting the information based on its classification must not be a consideration in the process of classifying the asset.

Primary and Secondary Asset (IT and non-IT Assets) classification must be documented before the start of the asset usage and accessible to relevant stakeholders, e.g., Information Owners, Asset Owner, Project Leads.
The adequacy of the information classification and any relevant documentation must be reviewed at least yearly and should be reviewed at the latest when risk assessment is performed.
It must be ensured that all critical or important functions and their supporting assets are identified.
Procedures to identify critical or important functions must be in place.
Critical or important functions must be identified and documented according to the specific criteria of the legal entities.

Primary and Secondary Assets supporting critical or important functions must be identified and documented together with their roles and dependencies in relation to ICT risk to provide context for the classification of information.
The identification of critical or important functions must be carried out at least annually.
It must be ensured that an ICT Risk Management Methodology is in place considering an ICT Risk Profile as input for the ICT Risk Management lifecycle.
An ICT Risk Management Methodology must be defined, operationalized, and implemented to specify the ICT Risk Management Processes, including ICT risk assessment and the flow of ICT risk information.

ICT Risk Management Methodology must consider the pre-defined ICT Risk Profile and include a measurement mechanism for the ICT risk level (considering the ICT Threat Landscape, Threat Events and Risk Categories).

ICT Risk Management Methodology must define guidance for the ICT Risk Management procedures on mechanisms to integrate information regarding the ICT Risk Profile (specifically threat insights) in the ICT risk management processes.
It must be ensured that ICT Risk Management processes are in place to identify, assess, treat, monitor, and report ICT risks.
ICT Risk Management processes (incl. tools) must be designed and implemented to ensure that the risks are adequately managed and within the defined risk appetite and tolerance level.

ICT Risk Management processes must reflect the ICT Risk Management Methodology (incl. consideration of an ICT Risk Profile which includes Risk Taxonomy, ICT Threat Landscape, ICT Risk Categories, etc.) and address managing of information security and information technology and other ICT-related risks (incl. facilities, people, and suppliers).
Risk acceptance criteria based on risk appetite as well as evaluation criteria and impact criteria must be defined.
All Primary (Information Assets, Process Assets) and Secondary Assets (IT and non-IT Assets) and control requirements must be part of the ICT Risk Management processes.
Appropriate ICT systems, protocols and tools must be used for managing ICT risks and related procedures and processes.

As part of the ICT Risk Management processes, relevant technological developments must be continuously monitored and their impact on the ICT risks, control requirements and digital operational resilience must be considered.

control_description: ICT Risk Management Roles and Responsibilities
control_requirement: It must be ensured that roles and responsibilities regarding ICT Risk Management and the resulting duties are defined, documented, and operated.

control_description: ICT Risk Management Roles and Responsibilities
control_requirement: Staff responsible for designing, managing, and operating the ICT Risk Management Framework must have the necessary skills and competence, gained through proper education, training, or experience, or be under the proper supervision of experienced staff to ensure effective ICT Risk management, IT and business operations, and IT compliance.

control_description: ICT Risk Management Roles and Responsibilities
control_requirement: Clearly separated roles and responsibilities considering the three lines of defense model or similar must be assigned for ICT-related functions such as for ICT Risk Oversight and ICT Operational Management, ensuring an appropriate level of independence between the roles to avoid conflict of interest.

control_description: ICT Risk Management Roles and Responsibilities
control_requirement: When outsourcing tasks to verify compliance with ICT Risk management requirements, whether internally or externally, DBAG or the respective legal entity remains fully accountable.

control_description: ICT Risk Management Roles and Responsibilities
control_requirement: An Information Owner and Asset Owner must be responsible to manage, monitor, protect and oversee information assets or IT and non-IT Assets throughout their entire lifecycle, ensuring the roles are identified, classified, maintained, and updated annually or in case of any changes.

control_description: ICT Risk Management Roles and Responsibilities
control_requirement: An Information Owner must ensure assessment and treatment of ICT risks for Primary and Secondary Assets throughout their entire lifecycle.

It must be ensured that all control requirements from ICT Risk Guidelines are fully addressed by controls, control ownership is assigned, controls are documented, and evidence from performed controls is in place.

Each control must be documented in relevant documents (e.g. Policies, Guidelines, Processes, Procedures, ICS or other supporting documentation aimed at addressing all aspects of control requirements).
Evidence of performed controls must be in place and available upon request.
Each control must have clearly defined ownership and be assigned to one Control Owner. Where this is not practicable, ownership may be assigned to multiple Control Owners. ●

control_description: ICT Risk Profile, ICT Threat Landscape and Risk Categories
control_requirement: It must be ensured that an ICT Risk Profile, including ICT Threat Landscape, and ICT Risk Categories are in place.

control_description: ICT Risk Profile, ICT Threat Landscape and Risk Categories
control_requirement: An ICT Risk Profile must be in place, including a collection of at least the following documentation, along with the links between these documents: The Risk Taxonomy, particularly the identification of the ICT-related Risk Clusters and relevant Risk Items (Level 4), the Risk Appetite for ICT risks (including Tolerance Levels), the ICT Threat Landscape, and ICT-related Operational Risk Scenarios (incl. results).

control_description: ICT Risk Profile, ICT Threat Landscape and Risk Categories
control_requirement: ICT-related entries in the Risk Taxonomy must be defined and operationalized based on external factors (e.g. industry best practices, external threat intelligence, regulatory requirements, etc.) and internal factors (e.g. business needs, risk appetite, internal threat intelligence).

control_description: ICT Risk Profile, ICT Threat Landscape and Risk Categories
control_requirement: The ICT-related risk appetite and tolerance levels must be defined and approved as part of the overall risk appetite and tolerance levels of DBAG, respectively the legal entities and in relation to the Risk Taxonomy.

control_description: ICT Risk Profile, ICT Threat Landscape and Risk Categories
control_requirement: The ICT-related entries to the Risk Taxonomy, ICT Threat Landscape, ICT Risk Categories, risk appetite and tolerance levels must be reviewed in defined intervals, at least annually.

control_description: ICT Risk Profile, ICT Threat Landscape and Risk Categories
control_requirement: An ICT Threat Landscape must be defined, refined, and implemented based on the pre-defined Risk Taxonomy and specifically identifying ICT threats to the Group Level.
